Output names and interpretation

Source: R/output-reference.R
crywolf-output.Rd

A reference for the parameter names and result fields returned by crywolf. Use help("crywolf-output") to open this page. Coefficients keep the same names in as_draws_df(fit), summary(fit)$table, and coef(fit).

Coefficient names

Suffixes come from the columns of R's stats::model.matrix(): (Intercept) for an intercept, the covariate name for a numeric slope, factor contrasts such as habitatforest, and interaction columns such as temp:rh. They refer to the covariate scale supplied to the fit; crywolf does not automatically standardize formula covariates.

NameMeaning and availability
occ_(Intercept), occ_<term>Coefficients of occ, on the logit scale of occupancy probability. Always present.
det_(Intercept), det_<term>Coefficients of det, on the logit scale of automated detection at occupied sites in the Miller design; in the Chambert design, of the true-detection component before combining true and false detections. Always present.
det_y_prevCoefficient of the previous automated detection when markov is supplied. A log odds change within the same site, not a transition in occupancy.
fp_(Intercept), fp_<term>Coefficients of fp, on the logit scale of the false-positive probability at unoccupied sites. Present when fp is not NULL.
verified_(Intercept), verified_<term>Coefficients of ver, on the logit scale of verified-method detection at occupied sites. Present only when verified occasions enter the fit.
fp_gapPositive difference det_(Intercept) - fp_(Intercept) on the logit scale. Present when fp is not NULL. It orders the reference intercepts, not all covariate-specific probabilities.
sd_recorderStandard deviation of the recorder random intercept on the detection logit scale, when the recorder effect is enabled.
sd_fp_siteStandard deviation of the site random intercept on the false-positive logit scale, when random_fp = TRUE.

coef(fit, "occ"), coef(fit, "det"), and coef(fit, "fp") select the corresponding prefixes. coef(fit, "fp") excludes fp_gap. coef(fit) returns posterior means of all readable draw variables, including derived probabilities and standard deviations.

Derived probabilities in posterior draws

Reference probabilities set design columns other than the intercept to zero and random effects to zero. This means the reference factor level under treatment contrasts, and y_prev = 0 under Markov detection. Reference values need not describe an observed site.

NameMeaning and availability
p11_refProbability of any automated detection at an occupied reference site. In Miller, plogis(det_(Intercept)). In Chambert, 1 - (1 - plogis(det_(Intercept))) * (1 - plogis(fp_(Intercept))). Always present.
p10_refplogis(fp_(Intercept)): false-positive probability at the reference covariates, with zero site effect. Present when fp is not NULL.
p10_barAverage false-positive probability over the fitted data, including fitted site effects. With site-level FP covariates, an unweighted mean over sites; with occasion-level FP covariates, a mean over unchecked automated occasions weighted by their trial counts. Confirmed occasions are excluded from this occasion average. Present when fp is not NULL.
p_verifiedplogis(verified_(Intercept)): verified-method detection probability at reference covariates, not an average over verified occasions. Present only with verified occasions.

When fp = NULL, false-positive probabilities are zero, but fp_*, p10_ref, and p10_bar are omitted from the readable draws. The Chambert observation-confirmation design requires a false-positive process; fp = NULL is rejected for that design.

Posterior summaries and fit diagnostics

summary(fit) returns table, prob, diagnostics, and call. Its table has one row per readable variable:

ColumnMeaning
variableReadable parameter or derived-quantity name.
mean, sdPosterior mean and standard deviation.
lower, upperEqual-tailed credible interval, with width prob.
rhatR-hat for this variable.
ess_bulk, ess_tailBulk and tail effective sample sizes.

fit$diagnostics contains divergences (total divergent transitions), max_treedepth (the number of transitions reaching the maximum depth, not the maximum depth observed), max_rhat (largest R-hat), min_ess_bulk, and min_ess_tail (smallest effective sample sizes). R-hat and the effective sample sizes are summarized across the readable variables; divergences and max_treedepth count sampler transitions.

Predictions and site estimates

predict(fit) appends estimate, lower, and upper to newdata: the posterior mean probability and equal-tailed interval for process. With summary = FALSE, it returns a matrix with posterior draws in rows and prediction rows in columns. These predictions use fixed effects; site or recorder random effects are not added or integrated out.

fp_effects() returns covariate, process, value (the covariate on the fitting scale), x (its display value after any transform), estimate, lower, and upper, with interval width in attribute prob.

fp_sites() retains the input site columns and adds:

ColumnMeaning
psi, psi_lower, psi_upperPosterior mean and interval for occupancy probability given site covariates.
occupied, occupied_lower, occupied_upperPosterior mean and interval of the probability of occupancy conditional on the site's observations and each parameter draw. The interval describes parameter uncertainty in that probability, not an interval for a binary state.
detectionsNumber of detections in unchecked automated occasions. Confirmed occasions are excluded.
verifiedWhether occupancy is certain from a verified detection or a confirmed true observation (Chambert). Despite the name, it includes both sources of evidence.
p10Posterior mean FP probability including the site's fitted random effect, if any. With occasion-level FP covariates, the trial-weighted average over the site's unchecked automated occasions. Present only with false positives.

For occasion-level FP covariates, the current implementation returns p10 = 0 for a site without unchecked automated occasions; this is an empty-data convention, not evidence for a zero false-positive rate.

Checks and threshold sweeps

fp_ppc() returns y (observed detection counts by retained site), yrep (replicated counts, draws by sites), fit_obs, fit_rep (discrepancies per draw), p_value (the proportion with fit_rep > fit_obs), site (retained identifiers), method, and fit_stat.

fp_prior_predictive() has columns naive_occupancy (share of all sites with an automated detection), automated_rate, verified_rate, mean_psi (mean occupancy probability), and p10_bar. Attribute observed holds the first three summaries for the observed data. Each row is one simulated dataset from the priors.

fp_threshold_sweep() has columns threshold, detection_rate (share of occasions detected), parameter (readable name), mean, lower, upper, divergences, and max_rhat. Attribute prob holds the interval width. Named threshold selection adds threshold_selection (one row per method) and validation_metrics (one row per candidate score): threshold, tp, fp, fn, precision, recall, and f1; threshold_selection also has method. Here fp is a false-positive count, not a model coefficient. See fp_threshold_sweep() for definitions.

Calibration and simulation

fp_calibrate() and fp_calibrate_fit() return cell, rep, seed, model, parameter, truth, mean, lower, upper, covered, divergences, max_rhat, ok, and seconds; fp_calibrate() adds the columns of its design. ok records whether fitting returned a result, not convergence. summary() groups by cell, model and parameter and returns the design columns plus n (successful fits), failed, coverage, mc_se (Monte Carlo standard error of coverage), bias, rmse, and prop_divergent (fraction of successful fits with divergences). fp_verification_curve() returns the calibration object invisibly; its printed curve selects model, frac_verified, coverage, mc_se, and bias for occ_x.

fp_sbc() returns rep, parameter, truth, rank (number of retained draws below the true value), divergences, and ok, with attribute ndraws. Its summary() returns parameter, n, mean_rank (mean rank divided by ndraws), p_uniform (chi-squared rank-histogram test p-value), and divergent (fraction with divergences); attribute failed counts failed replicates. In SBC only, parameter log_lik is the total log likelihood, rather than a site's contribution.

simulate_fp() returns data and truth. The latter records the generating arguments (psi, b1, p11, p10, r11, sigma_p10, p10_conc, conf_effect, conf_cor, a_bio, a_aci, sd_recorder, frac_confirmed), b0 (occupancy intercept), regime, conf_cor_realized, n_verified_sites, z (binary state by site), p10_site, and p10_marginal (mean of p10_site). simulate(fit) returns a list of datasets, each with data and truth; its truth fields are pars (named generating coefficients), z, p10_site, and p10_bar.

Readable draws and raw Stan names

The fitted object contains draws, fit (the backend fit), data, formulas, markov, random_recorder, random_fp, priors, sampler, diagnostics, call, design, and stan_data. sampler records chains, parallel_chains, threads_per_chain, iter_warmup, iter_sampling, and adapt_delta.

as_draws_df(fit) returns the readable variables above, with posterior metadata .chain, .iteration, and .draw. The backend's fit$fit$draws() also exposes raw Stan names. Current mappings are:

Stan nameReadable name
beta[k]occ_<term>
alpha[k]det_<term>
gamma0, gamma_fp[k]fp_(Intercept), fp_<term>
delta0, delta_s[k]verified_(Intercept), verified_<term>
r11p_verified
sigma_u, sigma_fp[1]sd_recorder, sd_fp_site

fp_gap, p11_ref, p10_ref, and p10_bar keep their names. log_lik[i] is the state-marginalized log likelihood of site i, in input site-table order; loo() uses sites as its pointwise units. It is available from fit$fit$draws("log_lik"), not the readable draws. With a fitted site random effect, state marginalization does not also integrate that effect out. Raw random effects (u, u_raw, e_raw) and sampler variable lp__ are backend outputs, not additional public coefficient names. design and stan_data describe internal encodings; their field names and raw Stan names are implementation details.
